transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-27 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Aisha Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Sharma (Starlight Med CDO), Michael Torres (Starlight VP Eng), Lina Gomez (Starlight Compliance)

Summary: Quick call to align on quality eval plan for POC; define success criteria (clinical correctness, hallucination rate, formatting), decide size of workload for benchmarks, and timelines for running regression tests.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, quick agenda: align on success criteria, golden prompts, workload size and timeline. Aisha will cover the benchmarking plan.
01:02 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Thanks, Jordan. Hi Priya, Michael, Lina. Quick context: Starlight wants to validate clinical answer accuracy and format adherence for our summarization and triage assistant. We're proposing a quality eval with golden prompts and regression tests.
03:15 Dr. Priya Sharma: Great, yeah accuracy and safety are top. For success criteria we need, um, clinical correctness at least 95% on our test set, hallucination rate below 2%, and strict PHI handling and redaction \u2014 can't return sensitive identifiers.
05:10 Michael Torres: Also latency and cost matter. We can't have >500ms p95 for single-turn triage callbacks. If Redwood Dedicated helps, we'd consider it, but need cost numbers.
07:20 Aisha: For benchmarks we recommend two phases: baseline run on hosted for 1k golden prompts to measure accuracy/formatting/cost; then a larger regression suite of 5-10k prompts that we run on rollouts and after model updates.
09:05 Lina Gomez: On compliance, we need audit logs, KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence. Also need DPA clauses. We'll review the security pack.
11:30 Speaker 1 (Jordan): On scoring: propose weighted rubric \u2014 60% clinical correctness (human review), 15% hallucination score (binary per-case flagged), 15% format compliance (structured fields, JSON schema pass), 10% latency/cost penalty. Does that align?
13:02 Dr. Priya Sharma: Yes, clinical correctness is the most important. For human review we'll sample 10% and use inter-rater agreement. If disagreement >10% we escalate.
15:40 Aisha: For golden prompts \u2014 ask Starlight to provide 200 canonical examples covering the top 20 intents and edge cases; we'll seed the golden set with those plus 800 synthetic prompts to reach 1k.
17:00 Michael Torres: What's the hallucination check look like? Are we doing exact-match to source docs or human label for fabricated facts?
18:40 Aisha: Good question. We do an automated fact-check step where possible (link to source in clinical KB), but many cases require human label. So hallucination rate will be a human-reviewed metric, automated flags help prioritize.
20:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): On format checks, we need JSON output that conforms to our triage schema \u2014 missing fields are failures. We also need section-level confidence scores if possible.
22:55 Speaker 2 (Aisha): We'll enforce schema validation with strict parser; formatting errors counted as failures in the format compliance metric.
25:00 Jordan: Workload sizing: for the initial POC we'll run 1k golden prompt baseline, 5k regression suite over 2 weeks. For ongoing monitoring, monthly 1k sample runs and continuous canary with 100/day.
27:30 Michael Torres: That sounds reasonable. For pilot timeline, we want to start tests week of 2026-04-06 and have results by 2026-04-13 so we can decide on Dedicated vs Hosted.
29:10 Lina Gomez: For Private deployment questions, we need to schedule a deeper session with infra to discuss VPC peering and HSM/KMS access.
31:45 Aisha: Benchmarks to run: accuracy (human-rated), hallucination (human + automated flagging), format validation (schema pass rate), latency (p50/p95), token cost estimates. We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet template.
34:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Scoring approach detail: each prompt gets a label (correct/incorrect), hallucination flag, format pass/fail, latency ms. We'll compute weighted score per prompt and aggregate. Pass threshold 85% weighted score for POC success.
36:30 Dr. Priya Sharma: Ok, can we include a few high-sensitivity edge cases where false positive triage could cause over-escalation? We need the model to be conservative.
38:00 Aisha: We'll prioritize those in the golden set and give them higher weight in the scoring or separate gating checks.
40:20 Michael Torres: On benchmarking infra \u2014 do we supply sample data and prompts to Redwood? Or do you simulate?
41:10 Jordan: Best is customer-supplied anonymized prompts + labels. If not possible, we can help synthesize but that has limitations for clinical nuance.
43:00 Speaker 2 (Aisha): Also note minor transcription thing: will send the benchmark harness link; the initial run will be done on a standard Redwood hosted model, then we can replicate on Dedicated or Private with same seeds.
44:35 Lina Gomez: Security items \u2014 we need retention policy options and ability to disable logging for PHI flows. Can you note those as requirements?
45:10 Jordan: Noted. We'll include options for short retention and logging off, and note any tradeoffs to debugging/observability.
47:25 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Recap of next steps: Jordan will send SOC2/security pack and pricing estimates; Aisha will run 1k baseline and share spreadsheet; Michael will provide 200 golden prompts + 500 sample prompts by 2026-03-31; Lina to confirm DPA questions by 2026-03-29.
49:00 Dr. Priya Sharma: Thanks, appreciate the clarity. we'll aim to review the results with execs after the April 13 report.
50:30 Speaker 2 (Aisha): I'll schedule the technical deep dive for Private deployment with infra for next week, pending your availability.
51:20 Meeting end.
